text:
I think this is good. a few things:

1. I had envisioned the beat where we are seeing the checkpoint from behind her shoulder on the right, like my right, not her right. I think maybe you confused that. the downside of the current approach is you don't see the alternative route since it's blocked by her head.
2. I think the checkpoint needs to be a bit further away, it's too close for the avoiding maneuvre to be believable. and when you work on the checkppint, I think we need to make a bit more...formidable. and the guards maybe need to be mounted on horses so they also look...formidable. and also perceivable at the distance.
3. Her expression when she realizes the danger is still too subtle. like i don't perceive anything at all.
4. I am noticing another thing now. her hair is perfectly still. it becomes especially obvious in the uphill gallop since we see her on the other side where strands of hair are hanging down to her neck, and they are not moving at all. I think we need some simulation.
5. I think you nailed the dramatic turn sequence. definitely the highlight of this sequence. we just have to make sure the viewer can see the checkpoint AND the alternative route as I said earlier, otherwise the dramatic turn doesn't make sense, it confuses. I think the beat where she recognizes the danger up ahead should be immediately followed by a glance towards the alternative route. and then when that is followed by the behind the shoulder camera, this time on the other side, it all adds up. 
6.
